# Balancer data-size policy and zone-aware migration — concept pack (small)

## How it works

- [statement] Adding, removing, or changing zones or zone ranges can trigger chunk migrations. The amount of affected data and chunks can affect cluster performance, so MongoDB recommends scheduling balancing windows. Defining zones and ranges before sharding an empty or nonexistent collection lets MongoDB create and initially distribute chunks using those zones. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sharding-tiered-hardware-for-varying-slas/ · keywords: Balancer data-size policy and zone-aware migration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/zone-sharding/, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/manage-the-apsaradb-for-mongodb-balancer
- [statement] Percona treats even workload distribution as a goal alongside even data distribution, while MongoDB describes the balancer's migration trigger in terms of collection data size (a difference of at least three times the configured range size). Sources: https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-new-balancer-policy-and-automerger/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/ — https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-new-balancer-policy-and-automerger/ · keywords: Balancer data-size policy and zone-aware migration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] Configured chunkSize affects the maximum amount of data the balancer attempts to migrate between two shards in a single chunk migration, but it is not a hard cap on stored chunk size: a sharded cluster only splits chunks when they must be migrated, so a chunk can exceed chunkSize (for example a 1 TB chunk with chunkSize 256 MB). Separately, MongoDB documents indivisible chunks (such as a range of a single shard key value) that cannot be split. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/clear-jumbo-flag/ — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/ · keywords: Balancer data-size policy and zone-aware migration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-data-partitioning/

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Starting in MongoDB 6.1, the balancer distributes sharded data by data size rather than number of chunks. The manual says a collection is balanced while its shard data-size difference is below three times the configured range size (chunkSize); at the default 128 MB, a difference of at least 384 MB is needed for a migration. Alibaba's ApsaraDB guide likewise reports a 384 MB trigger (three times the default chunk size) for MongoDB 6.0 instances, and notes that after upgrading to V6.0 (minor 7.0.1) or later, chunk counts may look unbalanced as expected behavior of the new balancer. Alibaba's separate troubleshooting page states the threshold behavior starts in MongoDB 6.0.3. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/release-notes/7.0/ ; https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/ ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/manage-the-apsaradb-for-mongodb-balancer ; https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/support/troubleshoot-mongodb-shard-data-imbalance — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/v7.0/release-notes/7.0/ · keywords: Balancer data-size policy and zone-aware migration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/use-cases/manage-the-apsaradb-for-mongodb-balancer, https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/mongodb/support/chunk-count-imbalance-after-mongodb-upgrade

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Zone ranges constrain migration destinations: a chunk whose shard-key range falls within a zone can migrate only to a shard assigned to that zone. A range outside all zones may reside on any shard. Zone placement is not instantaneous; until balancing completes, chunks can still violate newly configured zones. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/zone-sharding/ · keywords: Balancer data-size policy and zone-aware migration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sharding-tiered-hardware-for-varying-slas/, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/
- [statement] MongoDB's procedure for changing zones on an existing collection disables the balancer and waits for any active balancing round to finish before changing zone assignments and ranges; balancing is then re-enabled to move data into compliant locations. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-20) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/sharding-tiered-hardware-for-varying-slas/ · keywords: Balancer data-size policy and zone-aware migration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/
- [statement] MongoDB documents hardware and performance placement as a use for zones, but zone boundaries must use shard-key fields; with a compound shard key, a zone range must include the shard-key prefix. (medium confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/zone-sharding/ · keywords: Balancer data-size policy and zone-aware migration · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/sharding-balancer-administration/
- [statement] MongoDB's manual says zone sharding is unsupported for time-series collections, which the balancer instead distributes evenly across all shards. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-10-23) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/zone-sharding/
